topic: SQL, PostgreSQL, and Relational Data Modeling
learningObjectives: Explain relational databases, tables, keys, and relationships.
Design normalized database structures for application data.
Construct basic SQL operations for creating and querying data.

activities.title: Relational Database Anatomy
activities.instruction: Click each database element to explore its purpose.

content.concept: Relational databases organize structured data into tables made of rows and columns, with keys used to identify records and connect related tables.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: A structured collection of related records.
Defines an attribute or field for each record.
Represents one record in a table.
Uniquely identifies a record in a table.
Stores a reference to a key in another table to represent a relationship.

activities.title: Relationship Mapper
activities.instruction: Explore how different table relationships connect records.

content.concept: Relational databases represent one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many relationships using keys and, when necessary, junction tables.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: One record in one table is associated with one record in another table.
One record can be associated with many records in another table.
Records on both sides can have multiple related records, commonly represented using a junction table.

activities.title: SQL Operation Explorer
activities.instruction: Choose the SQL command that matches the requested operation.

content.concept: SQL provides commands such as SELECT for reading data, INSERT for creating rows, UPDATE for modifying rows, and DELETE for removing rows.

activities.title: Database Schema Builder
activities.instruction: Build a normalized schema for users and their orders.

content.concept: Normalization separates related data into focused tables and uses keys to maintain relationships while reducing unnecessary duplication.
